correctness.rationale: The Ewens partial-arrow contraction gives a two-arrow inversion probability and known Q_n. Condition on a specified fixed point and relabel: the remaining permutation has Ewens law on n-1 labels, with an exactly computable incident inversion expectation. Subtracting Q_n yields the quadratic position covariance and explicit H_n. The bracket defining H_n has fixed positive sign and determines the entire sign classification. Summation yields a rational aggregate covariance with manifestly positive polynomial bracket and overall negative sign. Exact rational enumeration checked 1672 assertions on n<=7 plus the full tensor to n<=6. The bounds n>=3 and theta>0 prevent singular denominators; the analytic proof, not bounded experiments, establishes the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The exact Ewens inversion probability and expected count are credited to Pinsky–Schickentanz (2025), and general local/conjugacy-class methods to Hamaker–Rhoades and Campion Loth et al. The checked published results do not state the selected-index fixed-point mixed covariance tensor, its inside/outside inversion-gap sign boundary, the exact central positive-window versus always-negative aggregate classification, or the n^-1 near-uniform crossover. These are new explicit dependence conclusions, although logically derived using known marginal formulas and standard fixed-point deletion; historical implicit coverage is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier broad permutation class-function or generating-function computation may implicitly contain the same selected-index mixed moments; mere absence of a literal formula in inspected sections is not proof of first priority.

Exact formulas can be deduced from the 2025 marginal inversion mean and the classical deletion property; the novelty claim is limited to a motivated complete explicit sign/scale classification, not the underlying basic tools.
Selected sections of some sources, rather than every page of every relevant monograph, were inspected; latent coverage cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The exact finite-n dependence classification exposes a counterintuitive positive O(sqrt(n))-position central region for 0<theta<1 even while the global fixed-point/inversion covariance is negative of order n; it also identifies a universal theta=1 sign boundary, inside/outside inversion-gap change and a fine theta=1-lambda/n window. These are natural, cross-statistic structural questions that marginal inversion results and asymptotic descent limits do not determine. Their motivating object is the signed mixed dependence between local cycle structure and a global ordering statistic, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
